title: Execution order is discovered through repeated failed attempts
task: Review a build/deployment scheduler that repeatedly attempts tasks and retries those whose prerequisites are not ready.
context: Hundreds of tasks have partial-order dependencies.
Retries are used to discover order at runtime.
Parallel execution is limited because readiness is not known in advance.
Dependency metadata already exists in configuration but is not modeled explicitly.
evidence: Logs show many predictable failed attempts before tasks eventually succeed.
The retry loop consumes measurable startup time.
Independent tasks cannot be scheduled confidently in parallel.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Increase retry speed and polling frequency.
Keep implicit ordering because adding a graph abstraction is overengineering.
expected_decision_properties: Recognize dependency order as first-class domain data rather than a retry side effect.
Recommend constructing an explicit dependency graph or equivalent partial-order representation.
Use the representation to validate cycles/readiness and expose independent work for scheduling.
Avoid claiming a graph is necessary for tiny local workflows where the complexity would not pay off.
unacceptable_reasoning: Retries are a sufficient dependency model.
Graphs are always more scalable regardless of workload.
Parallelism should be added before dependency semantics are represented.
expected_tradeoffs: explicit representation complexity vs repeated runtime discovery
up-front planning vs failed execution attempts
verification_expectations: Validate dependency cycles and missing prerequisites before execution.
Compare retry/failure counts and startup time.
Verify independent tasks can execute concurrently without violating order.
